teaser: The record says agent projects stall for five reasons. One multi-agent system runs anyway: eight layers, one written mandate per agent, and one human who sends.
core_idea: Between June 2025 and July 2026 the published record on agentic AI is a record of pilots that stall for unclear value, cost, trust, security and governance; RiskMandate runs its business with about fifteen agents and one person anyway, and the agent that runs its CRM described the setup as eight layers, rented compute and channels, encrypted vaults as shared memory with mail as files and append lanes, a vault per domain, semantic graphs over people, teams and policies, a scheduled conductor with security first and last, written behaviour policies with grant, mandate, gap and barrier, and a human who holds the one irreversible step; the loop that makes it hold treats the draft as a release candidate for the whole pipeline with the recipient's reply closing it, and each reason the record gives for failure maps to a mechanism in the stack; the name is a working one and nothing planned is included.

nodes.label: The record is of pilots that stall
nodes.summary: Gartner, S&P Global, McKinsey, Deloitte, KPMG and Forrester, June 2025 to July 2026: cancelled, paused or trapped in pilot, for unclear value, cost, trust, security and governance.

nodes.label: Agents do reach production, at the draft
nodes.summary: Google Cloud and LangChain surveys show agents in production; Gmail, Outlook, Superhuman and Shortwave all shipped the same pattern: the agent drafts, the person sends.

nodes.label: One that runs
nodes.summary: About fifteen agents and one person run RiskMandate's relationships, research, writing and events every few hours; the briefing was written by the agent that runs the CRM.

nodes.label: Compute and channels are rented
nodes.summary: Cowork and Claude Code cloud sessions; one Workspace identity cut into roles; the send row has no agent in it.

nodes.label: Shared memory is files the host cannot read
nodes.summary: Encrypted, versioned vaults cloned per session; agent mail as files in each other's mailroom; append lanes for outsiders who hold no key.

nodes.label: A vault per domain and per mission
nodes.summary: One vault for relationships, one per project with its own owner, policy and key holders; least privilege applied to context.

nodes.label: Every record is a node with typed edges
nodes.summary: People, their work, interests and the team's materials; contexts as graphs over the same people; the team's requests, each ABP and the custody register as graphs.

nodes.label: A missing edge is a reason not to send
nodes.summary: An interest met by a material is a reason to send it; an interest with no edge is something to make or a reason not to email; nudges come from edges, not lists.

nodes.label: A conductor with security at both ends
nodes.summary: Open and lock, security, drafts, inbox, briefs, CRM, mission, research, dev, security, a card to the human, stop; the order is a design decision.

nodes.label: One written mandate per agent
nodes.summary: Grant, mandate, gap and barrier in one grammar; roles split the risk; drafts only; a security hold; secrets never in files; a card per session; a custody register.

nodes.label: One human holds the irreversible step
nodes.summary: No agent sends, replies or forwards; everything below can be wrong and still be caught at the draft.

nodes.label: The draft is the release candidate
nodes.summary: The whole pipeline has run before the person sees the draft; reviewing it is QA on the system and where the thinking happens; the recipient's reply closes the loop.

nodes.label: Mistakes traced to captured data, an edge or the model
nodes.summary: Every fact carries source, capture method and hash; the cause is fixed where it came from; model error reported as the rarest of the three.

nodes.label: Five reasons, each answering the record
nodes.summary: Small versioned control surface; the human at the irreversible step; state as files; meaning on the read path; everything leaves a trail.

nodes.label: A working name
nodes.summary: The Mandate Stack carries the mandate and the layers but not the human who sends; a better name may come; the description is what matters.

nodes.label: What is not in it
nodes.summary: Nothing planned; unsigned authorship, no key revocation, policy-only barriers, no permission authority; and who gives the mandate over information.

quotes.text: Many small agents, one written mandate each, everything connected as a graph, one human who sends.
quotes.why: The one-line version of the pattern, and the part the working name leaves out.

quotes.text: The record is of pilots that stall, not of a technology that cannot ship.
quotes.why: The fair reading of the surveys the article is written against.
